entities.summary: Liu Ling, a Chinese poet and scholar, played a pivotal role in the literary and intellectual landscape of the Classical era (221-300 CE). Born in 221 CE, Liu Ling's life was marked by his prolific output of poetry and his involvement in the development of the Confucian classics. His most notable contribution was the compilation of the 'Ling Shu', a comprehensive treatise on Confucian philosophy. This work cemented Liu Ling's status as one of the most important scholars of his time, solidifying his legacy as a key figure in the transmission of Confucian thought. Despite his significant influence, Liu Ling's personal life remains somewhat of a mystery, with little information available about his family background or later life. Nevertheless, his enduring impact on Chinese literature and philosophy ensures his place among the most notable figures of the Classical era.
